title: Weekly commerce review and Monday trading note
company: Northgate Goods, a fictional DTC kitchen and home brand on Shopify
question: Why did contribution margin fall while orders grew?
summary: Shopify, ad platforms, email and 3PL billing joined into contribution after advertising, by channel and week. The Monday note explains what moved the margin, in order of impact.

title: Portfolio KPI pack for operating partners
company: Ridgeline Partners Fund II, a fictional fund with five portfolio companies on five accounting systems
question: Which companies need attention this month, and can we trust the numbers?
summary: Five trial balances from NetSuite, QuickBooks, Xero, Sage Intacct and SAP mapped to one chart of accounts, with covenant headroom, an EBITDA bridge and data-quality checks that block sign-off.

title: Month-end management pack with variance commentary
company: Harbour Foods, a fictional food manufacturer in the same portfolio
question: Why is EBITDA behind budget, and is anything missing from the numbers?
summary: Actual against budget for the month and year to date, built from the mapped trial balance. Costs on unmapped accounts are shown on their own line instead of disappearing from EBITDA.

title: Plant scorecard and weekly exception digest
company: Keystone Precision Components, a fictional contract machine shop (6 CNC machines, 3 shifts)
question: Where is the plant losing capacity, and what are operators telling us that the codes miss?
summary: OEE built from first principles out of MES shift data, a downtime Pareto, on-time-in-full by customer, and operator notes classified by AI so that symptoms logged as 'OTHER' are not lost.

title: ARR bridge, retention and renewal risk
company: Lumenly, a fictional B2B SaaS company (~$15.5M ARR)
buyer: CFO, VP Revenue, head of customer success
question: Where is retention slipping, what revenue is missing from billing, and which renewals are at risk?
summary: Billing as the source of truth for ARR, reconciled against CRM deals, with retention by segment and a transparent renewal-risk score built from product usage and support tickets.

title: Freight invoice audit and dispute drafts
company: Brookline Distribution, a fictional distributor shipping with four carriers
question: Are carriers billing what the contract says?
summary: Every invoiced shipment re-priced against the contracted rate card, fuel terms and requested accessorials. Discrepancies are classified, totalled by carrier and turned into dispute drafts.

title: Book-of-business dashboard and AI submission intake
company: Ashgrove Specialty, a fictional MGA writing commercial lines
question: Where is the book deteriorating, and can submission intake be automated without silent errors?
summary: Loss ratio, retention and claims aging from policy and claims data, plus an extraction workflow that reads broker submissions, scores its own confidence and routes anything uncertain to a person.

title: Retail analytics at scale: 2.3M order lines, eight report pages
company: Contoso (fictional electronics retailer: 73 stores plus online)
buyer: CEO, CFO, head of retail and e-commerce
question: Why did sales fall in 2025 when order volume barely moved?
summary: A full retail model on the public Contoso sample: 2,349,091 order lines, 104,990 customers and 2,517 products over 2016-2025, modelled in dbt and reported in Power BI, with an AI-drafted annual review checked against the numbers.
